public_rationale: Independent results show substantial success on elementary mathematical word problems, alongside failures on college engineering problems. Neither establishes the broad claim as written. Treating any error as unreliability would impose an unstated perfection standard; treating success on GSM8K as proof across simple science problems would also overreach.
limitations: Task selection and prompting materially affect the results.
The cited elementary benchmark evaluates Code Interpreter, not Wolfram Alpha.
The authors' own bespoke evaluation is excluded as independent outcome evidence.

our_interpretation: The preceding discussion makes this a claim about GPT-4 with Code Interpreter or Wolfram Alpha.
The plain reading is that users cannot depend on consistently correct solutions across ordinary simple word problems; it does not require literal perfection.
Use the 2023 model generation as the reporting period, restricted to evaluations conducted before October 23. No regular reporting interval is specified.
Separate ordinary single-answer use from additional verification and repeated-sampling methods.
criteria.support_condition: Representative tests of simple word problems show recurring material failures with the named plug-ins under ordinary use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative tests show consistently dependable solutions across simple mathematical and scientific word problems with the named plug-ins.

evidence.excerpt: In particular, OpenAI's latest version of GPT-4, known as GPT-4 Code Interpreter, shows remarkable performance on challenging math datasets.
evidence.explanation: The paper reports 92.9% GSM8K accuracy for baseline Code Interpreter and 97.0% with verification and voting. This is material evidence against a sweeping claim of poor elementary-word-problem performance, but it does not establish reliability across scientific problems or Wolfram Alpha.

evidence.excerpt: The performance of all versions of ChatGPT is somewhat stochastic.
evidence.publisher: arXiv; Tanuj Kumar and Mikhail A. Kats
evidence.explanation: The repeated-trial study found uneven Code Interpreter accuracy, while its easiest problems were solved in every reported trial and consensus answers succeeded on all 13 problems. Its college engineering scope and lack of Wolfram Alpha testing prevent direct resolution of the broader simple-problem claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent pre-post tests of both plug-in systems on representative simple mathematical and scientific word problems, with repeated trials, documented errors, and a defensible reliability standard.
